title: ATM requirements and scope
idea: Scoping an ATM system means naming who uses it, what they can do, the money rule that must never break, and what v1 leaves out.
points: A customer inserts a card, enters a PIN, checks balance and withdraws cash.
The core rule: cash leaves the machine only if the account was debited.
Limits apply per withdrawal and per day, enforced by the bank for every ATM.
Assume many ATMs share one bank; two ATMs may use one account at once.

edges.caption: Every session starts with a card and a PIN. Three wrong PINs and the card is kept.
Once authenticated, the customer can read the balance. Nothing changes.
Withdrawal is the risky use case: the bank debits money and the machine hands out notes.

edges.label: refills
edges.caption: An operator loads note cassettes. The ATM can only pay amounts its notes can make.

edges.label: reverses
edges.caption: The system is an actor too: if notes jam after a debit, it credits the money back.
Deposits, transfers and PIN change wait for a later version. Say the cut out loud.

code.title: Scope and limits as code
code.caption: Use cases tagged IN or OUT of v1, and the withdrawal rules checked in a fixed order. The limit values are stated assumptions.

walk.text: Money is `long` paise. The two limits are assumptions you state, not facts.
Print each use case with its actor and whether v1 includes it.
Check four amounts against an account that already took Rs 20,000 today.
The ATM holds only whole notes, so the amount must be a multiple of Rs 100.
Then the per-withdrawal cap, then the daily total including this amount.

pitfalls: Do not jump to classes before agreeing which use cases are in v1.
Keep the daily limit at the bank; one ATM cannot see another ATM's withdrawals.
Forgetting the System actor hides the reversal flow until the failure case appears.

quiz.q: Where should the daily withdrawal limit be enforced?
options: In the screen, before the request is sent
At the bank, for every ATM together
In the cash dispenser, by counting notes
quiz.why: A customer can visit two ATMs in one day. Only the bank sees all withdrawals for the account, so only it can add them up.

takeaway: No cash without a debit; limits live at the bank, not the machine.
